result.keywords: AbstractThis meta-analysis examines the effectiveness of digital game-based vocabulary learning when embedded in science-oriented instructional contexts. The review compares gameplay-focused designs with game-mechanism enriched variants and evaluates moderating factors including educational level, learning stage, game platform, and scenario design. Overall, results indicate a moderate positive effect for game-integrated vocabulary instruction and a smaller but significant effect for mechanism-rich implementations. Subgroup analyses suggest benefits across learner levels, with stronger gains in settings that combine contextualized science content, guided interaction, and adaptive feedback. The findings also show that native-language background and instructional alignment can influence outcomes, while platform differences appear less pronounced. Implications point to carefully designed educational games that balance language practice with science concept support.
result.title: A meta-analysis of digital game-based vocabulary learning in science contexts
